stem: Let alpha be a covector on R^3 given by alpha(x, y, z) = 2x - z, and let v = (1, 5, 4). What is alpha(v), and why?
options: A. (2, 0, -1) - a covector applied to a vector returns a vector in the same space
B. -2 - evaluate the linear functional at v: 2(1) - 4
C. 6 - add the components of v that alpha mentions: 1 + 5
D. 2 - a covector reads off the coefficient of its first term

distractor_misconceptions.A: a covector is just a vector written sideways, so applying it returns a vector rather than a scalar
distractor_misconceptions.C: a covector sums the vector's components rather than evaluating a linear map
distractor_misconceptions.D: a covector reads off a single coordinate and ignores its own coefficients
